scope: Selected Old Babylonian Nippur evidence; qualifications in main report

claims.title: Hire mediated through a father
claims.claim: BE 6/2 51 records Idin-Ištar, explicitly the son of Nabi-Šamaš, hired from Nabi-Šamaš by Lu-Ninsianna for a fixed term with a monthly grain payment.
claims.context: Nippur legal document; Istanbul Ni 1847; no room-level context established
claims.primary: BE 6/2 51, Ni 1847; P1909 p. 43; catalogue p. 151. Monthly amount: 80 qa of grain in the edition.
claims.secondary: Poebel’s suggestion of payment at the end of the term is commentary, not an explicit clause.
claims.counter: The occupation, age, residence, precise payment recipient, and ownership status are not stated.
claims.rationale: The hiring parties, kin relation, term, and rate are explicit in the published text; confidence is confined to those particulars.
claims.limit: One hire agreement; not a standard wage, a census of hired workers, or proof of child labor or free self-contracting.
claims.relevance: A kin relationship and a paid work arrangement appear together without becoming the same relationship.
claims.interpretations: The father mediates the agreement. Whether he exercised ownership, guardianship, household authority, or another legal capacity cannot be decided from these clauses alone.

claims.title: Kinship and maintenance obligations
claims.claim: Nippur agreements connect filial or adoptive relationships with inheritance-linked maintenance obligations; these are not identical to ownership of the obligated person.
claims.context: BE 6/2 28: Ibkuša and two sons; BE 6/2 48: Awilia, Naramtum, and three sons; Nippur
claims.secondary: P1909 discusses maintenance and adoption together. The report retains the clauses without adopting a universal old-age explanation.
claims.counter: Maintenance supplies do not identify who produced them. Birth/adoptive relations do not establish age or co-residence.
claims.rationale: Two independently identified documents explicitly tie support and property expectations to filial relationships.
claims.limit: The specified agreements, not all adopted persons, all sons, or all household labor.
claims.relevance: Distinguishes support obligations and created kinship from enslavement and occupational work.
claims.interpretations: BE 28 places the son by the wife and the adopted son under parallel support duties. BE 48 gives Naramtum a filial relationship with Awilia’s sons and provides maintenance with property-related sanctions.

claims.title: Enslaved people in estate allocation
claims.claim: BE 6/2 23 allocates four named enslaved people between the shares of Narubtum and Ur-Pabilsaĝa.
claims.context: Nippur; Ur-Pabilsaĝa/interconnected family dossier; Istanbul Ni 1917
claims.etype: Primary edition, with modern disagreement check
claims.primary: BE 6/2 23, P1909 pp. 20–22; catalogue p. 147. Ali-aḫuša and Iškur-rīm-ilī in Narubtum’s portion; Dumqi-Ištar and Taribum in Ur-Pabilsaĝa’s.
claims.secondary: VW2018 pp. 21–22 records competing reconstructions of the closing kinship/adoption clause.
claims.counter: The contested genealogy does not erase the allocations. The text does not assign these people particular jobs or identify their own family ties.
claims.rationale: The named people and their allocation are explicit; the narrow claim does not require choosing the disputed genealogy.
claims.limit: A property division, not a headcount of co-residents or an occupational roster; no transfer itinerary established.
claims.relevance: Shows ownership interests passing through family property arrangements while residence and labor remain unrecorded.
claims.interpretations: Enslavement is supported by the legal allocation context, not by treating the gender designations alone as universally equivalent to “slave.”

claims.title: Conditional enslavement is not an accomplished sale
claims.claim: BE 6/2 24 stipulates sale following adoptees’ repudiation of their adoptive parents; the clause does not report that repudiation or sale occurred.
claims.context: Nippur; Ea-idinnam, Kuritum, Ili-idinnam, and Ili-ummati; CBS 10891, P266084
claims.primary: BE 6/2 24, P1909 pp. 27–29; catalogue p. 148. Additional conditional language is present in BE 6/2 57.
claims.secondary: P1909’s translation distinguishes the adoption from future breach conditions.
claims.counter: No enforcement event is documented in this text; it does not establish prior enslaved status.
claims.rationale: The conditional syntax and the completed adoption are different parts of the agreement.
claims.limit: Not a citywide rule that every adopted person was enslaved or every breach was actually punished this way.
claims.relevance: A status-changing sanction must remain distinct from a person’s status when the contract was drawn up.
claims.interpretations: The contract creates heirs and threatens a coercive consequence for a specified breach. Those facts should not be collapsed into one status lab
